source_note: MIT OpenCourseWare Calendar page (https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/24-261-philosophy-of-love-in-the-western-world-fall-2004/pages/calendar/) for titles/order, cross-checked with the Syllabus and Video Lectures pages; fetched 2026-10-21. The four OCW-recorded video sessions are listed only as 'Session 1-4' with no titles or calendar mapping.

lectures.title: Introduction
lectures.summary: Opening session of the seminar, which the syllabus describes as a study of the nature of love and sex approached as topics in both philosophy and literature; the assigned reading is Irving Singer's 'Marriage: Same-Sex and Opposite-Sex' from Sex: A Philosophical Primer.

lectures.title: Irving Singer, The Pursuit of Love, pp. ix-43
lectures.summary: Seminar discussion of the opening pages (ix-43) of Irving Singer's philosophical study The Pursuit of Love.

lectures.title: Irving Singer, The Pursuit of Love, pp. 44-107
lectures.summary: Continuation of the seminar's discussion of Singer's The Pursuit of Love, covering pages 44-107.

lectures.title: Irving Singer, The Pursuit of Love, pp. 108-176
lectures.summary: Concluding session on Singer's The Pursuit of Love, covering pages 108-176.

lectures.title: Joseph Bédier, The Romance of Tristan and Iseult
lectures.summary: Discussion of Joseph Bédier's The Romance of Tristan and Iseult, read in its entirety as one of the classic literary myths of love that the course analyzes philosophically.

lectures.title: Friedrich Nietzsche, The Birth of Tragedy and The Case of Wagner, pp. 17-56, 139-92; Wagner excerpts; film: Pierre Jourdan, Tristan und Isolde (1974)
lectures.summary: Selected pages of Nietzsche's The Birth of Tragedy and The Case of Wagner together with Wagner excerpts, paired with an in-class screening of Pierre Jourdan's 1974 film production of the opera Tristan und Isolde.

lectures.title: Molière, Don Juan; Irving Singer, 'Two Essays on the Don Juan Myth in Molière'
lectures.summary: Discussion of Molière's play Don Juan, read in its entirety, together with Irving Singer's 'Two Essays on the Don Juan Myth in Molière.'

lectures.title: George Bernard Shaw, Man and Superman (Preface and 'Don Juan in Hell,' Act III)
lectures.summary: Discussion of the Preface and the 'Don Juan in Hell' scene from Act III of Shaw's Man and Superman, continuing the seminar's treatment of the Don Juan myth.

lectures.title: George Bernard Shaw, Pygmalion (with Preface and Afterword); film: Pygmalion (1938)
lectures.summary: Discussion of Shaw's Pygmalion, read in its entirety including Preface and Afterword, with an in-class screening of the 1938 Asquith and Howard film adaptation; the first paper is due at this lecture.

lectures.title: Irving Singer, Explorations in Love and Sex, pp. 105-67
lectures.summary: Seminar discussion of pages 105-67 of Irving Singer's Explorations in Love and Sex.

lectures.title: Irving Singer, Explorations in Love and Sex, pp. ix-xiii, 1-45
lectures.summary: Seminar discussion of the opening pages (ix-xiii, 1-45) of Singer's Explorations in Love and Sex.

lectures.title: Irving Singer, Explorations in Love and Sex, pp. 47-104, 217-24
lectures.summary: Final session on Singer's Explorations in Love and Sex, covering pages 47-104 and 217-24; the second paper is due at this lecture.
